newsitem.title: UK: Mideast crude tankers slower, but market firm.
newsitem.headline: Mideast crude tankers slower, but market firm.

text.p: Crude tanker chartering slowed on Friday in the Middle East Gulf after a busy week. Despite the slower pace of fixing rates consolidated around last done levels and may firm next week, brokers said.

Asian charterers continued to dominate with no tankers seen fixed westwards. Shipping brokers said rates out of the Middle East Gulf on VLCCs to Japan were steady around W60, with South Korea and Singapore a couple of points behind.
The lack of westbound chartering meant VLCCs heading to Europe and the U.S. have been unable to command higher rates unlike their sister ships heading to Asia.
Trips to the U.S. Gulf can still be secured around W52.5.
With modern tonnage becoming thin brokers expect the premium on newer tankers to increase, although owners of older ships may accepting lower rates in order to get their vessels fixed.

Brokers E.A. Gibson estimate 18.5 million tonnes will become available in the region over the next four weeks and that since only a dozen of the 64 vessels will be modern the indications are for further rate gains.
In the U.K/continent there were some aframaxes (80,000 tonners) finding employment with rates stuck at W102.5-105.

Little change was expected next week since tonnage supplies remain good. Glencore was seen taking the London Splendour to carry 130,000 tonnes transatlantic at W80, a good market indicative rate, brokers said.

The Mediterranean saw good interest for suezmaxes, but scant demand for 80,000 tonners. Rates were assessed around W100, although brokers said a dearth of enquiry would knock rates to W90. Suezmaxes were put around W80.
West African chartering continued healthy for owners with a VLCC taken by Koch to the U.S. Gulf at W62.5 and 130,000 tonners finding work to the U.S. around the W82.5-85 level.
